NASB.1: Moreover, from the blue and purple and scarlet [material], they made finely woven garments for ministering in the holy place as well as the holy garments which were for Aaron, just as the LORD had commanded Moses.
NASB.2: He made the ephod of gold, [and] of blue and purple and scarlet [material], and fine twisted linen.
NASB.3: Then they hammered out gold sheets and cut [them] into threads to be woven in [with] the blue and the purple and the scarlet [material], and the fine linen, the work of a skillful workman.
NASB.4: They made attaching shoulder pieces for the ephod; it was attached at its two [upper] ends.
NASB.5: The skillfully woven band which was on it was like its workmanship, of the same material: of gold [and] of blue and purple and scarlet [material], and fine twisted linen, just as the LORD had commanded Moses.
NASB.6: They made the onyx stones, set in gold filigree [settings]; they were engraved [like] the engravings of a signet, according to the names of the sons of Israel.
NASB.7: And he placed them on the shoulder pieces of the ephod, [as] memorial stones for the sons of Israel, just as the LORD had commanded Moses.
NASB.8: He made the breastpiece, the work of a skillful workman, like the workmanship of the ephod: of gold [and] of blue and purple and scarlet [material] and fine twisted linen.
NASB.9: It was square; they made the breastpiece folded double, a span long and a span wide when folded double.
NASB.10: And they mounted four rows of stones on it. The first row [was] a row of ruby, topaz, and emerald;
NASB.11: and the second row, a turquoise, a sapphire and a diamond;
NASB.12: and the third row, a jacinth, an agate, and an amethyst;
NASB.13: and the fourth row, a beryl, an onyx, and a jasper. They were set in gold filigree [settings] when they were mounted.
NASB.14: The stones were corresponding to the names of the sons of Israel; they were twelve, corresponding to their names, [engraved with] the engravings of a signet, each with its name for the twelve tribes.
NASB.15: They made on the breastpiece chains like cords, of twisted cordage work in pure gold.
NASB.16: They made two gold filigree [settings] and two gold rings, and put the two rings on the two ends of the breastpiece.
NASB.17: Then they put the two gold cords in the two rings at the ends of the breastpiece.
NASB.18: They put the [other] two ends of the two cords on the two filigree [settings], and put them on the shoulder pieces of the ephod at the front of it.
NASB.19: They made two gold rings and placed [them] on the two ends of the breastpiece, on its inner edge which was next to the ephod.
NASB.20: Furthermore, they made two gold rings and placed them on the bottom of the two shoulder pieces of the ephod, on the front of it, close to the place where it joined, above the woven band of the ephod.
NASB.21: They bound the breastpiece by its rings to the rings of the ephod with a blue cord, so that it would be on the woven band of the ephod, and that the breastpiece would not come loose from the ephod, just as the LORD had commanded Moses.
NASB.22: Then he made the robe of the ephod of woven work, all of blue;
NASB.23: and the opening of the robe was [at the top] in the center, as the opening of a coat of mail, with a binding all around its opening, so that it would not be torn.
NASB.24: They made pomegranates of blue and purple and scarlet [material and] twisted [linen] on the hem of the robe.
NASB.25: They also made bells of pure gold, and put the bells between the pomegranates all around on the hem of the robe,
NASB.26: alternating a bell and a pomegranate all around on the hem of the robe for the service, just as the LORD had commanded Moses.
NASB.27: They made the tunics of finely woven linen for Aaron and his sons,
NASB.28: and the turban of fine linen, and the decorated caps of fine linen, and the linen breeches of fine twisted linen,
NASB.29: and the sash of fine twisted linen, and blue and purple and scarlet [material], the work of the weaver, just as the LORD had commanded Moses.
NASB.30: They made the plate of the holy crown of pure gold, and inscribed it like the engravings of a signet, 'Holy to the LORD.'
NASB.31: They fastened a blue cord to it, to fasten it on the turban above, just as the LORD had commanded Moses.
NASB.32: Thus all the work of the tabernacle of the tent of meeting was completed; and the sons of Israel did according to all that the LORD had commanded Moses; so they did.
NASB.33: They brought the tabernacle to Moses, the tent and all its furnishings: its clasps, its boards, its bars, and its pillars and its sockets;
NASB.34: and the covering of rams' skins dyed red, and the covering of porpoise skins, and the screening veil;
NASB.35: the ark of the testimony and its poles and the mercy seat;
NASB.36: the table, all its utensils, and the bread of the Presence;
NASB.37: the pure [gold] lampstand, with its arrangement of lamps and all its utensils, and the oil for the light;
NASB.38: and the gold altar, and the anointing oil and the fragrant incense, and the veil for the doorway of the tent;
NASB.39: the bronze altar and its bronze grating, its poles and all its utensils, the laver and its stand;
NASB.40: the hangings for the court, its pillars and its sockets, and the screen for the gate of the court, its cords and its pegs and all the equipment for the service of the tabernacle, for the tent of meeting;
NASB.41: the woven garments for ministering in the holy place and the holy garments for Aaron the priest and the garments of his sons, to minister as priests.
NASB.42: So the sons of Israel did all the work according to all that the LORD had commanded Moses.
NASB.43: And Moses examined all the work and behold, they had done it; just as the LORD had commanded, this they had done. So Moses blessed them.

ESV.1: From the blue and purple and scarlet yarns they made finely woven garments,  for ministering in the Holy Place. They made the holy garments for Aaron, as the LORD had commanded Moses.
ESV.2: He made the ephod of gold, blue and purple and scarlet yarns, and fine twined linen.
ESV.3: And they hammered out gold leaf, and he cut it into threads to work into the blue and purple and the scarlet yarns, and into the fine twined linen, in skilled design.
ESV.4: They made for the ephod attaching shoulder pieces, joined to it at its two edges.
ESV.5: And the skillfully woven band on it was of one piece with it and made like it, of gold, blue and purple and scarlet yarns, and fine twined linen, as the LORD had commanded Moses.
ESV.6: They made the onyx stones, enclosed in settings of gold filigree, and engraved like the engravings of a signet, according to the names of the sons of Israel.
ESV.7: And he set them on the shoulder pieces of the ephod to be stones of remembrance for the sons of Israel, as the LORD had commanded Moses.
ESV.8: He made the breastpiece, in skilled work, in the style of the ephod, of gold, blue and purple and scarlet yarns, and fine twined linen.
ESV.9: It was square. They made the breastpiece doubled, a span  its length and a span its breadth when doubled.
ESV.10: And they set in it four rows of stones. A row of sardius, topaz, and carbuncle was the first row;
ESV.11: and the second row, an emerald, a sapphire, and a diamond;
ESV.12: and the third row, a jacinth, an agate, and an amethyst;
ESV.13: and the fourth row, a beryl, an onyx, and a jasper. They were enclosed in settings of gold filigree.
ESV.14: There were twelve stones with their names according to the names of the sons of Israel. They were like signets, each engraved with its name, for the twelve tribes.
ESV.15: And they made on the breastpiece twisted chains like cords, of pure gold.
ESV.16: And they made two settings of gold filigree and two gold rings, and put the two rings on the two edges of the breastpiece.
ESV.17: And they put the two cords of gold in the two rings at the edges of the breastpiece.
ESV.18: They attached the two ends of the two cords to the two settings of filigree. Thus they attached it in front to the shoulder pieces of the ephod.
ESV.19: Then they made two rings of gold, and put them at the two ends of the breastpiece, on its inside edge next to the ephod.
ESV.20: And they made two rings of gold, and attached them in front to the lower part of the two shoulder pieces of the ephod, at its seam above the skillfully woven band of the ephod.
ESV.21: And they bound the breastpiece by its rings to the rings of the ephod with a lace of blue, so that it should lie on the skillfully woven band of the ephod, and that the breastpiece should not come loose from the ephod, as the LORD had commanded Moses.
ESV.22: He also made the robe of the ephod woven all of blue,
ESV.23: and the opening of the robe in it was like the opening in a garment, with a binding around the opening, so that it might not tear.
ESV.24: On the hem of the robe they made pomegranates of blue and purple and scarlet yarns and fine twined linen.
ESV.25: They also made bells of pure gold, and put the bells between the pomegranates all around the hem of the robe, between the pomegranates —
ESV.26: a bell and a pomegranate, a bell and a pomegranate around the hem of the robe for ministering, as the LORD had commanded Moses.
ESV.27: They also made the coats, woven of fine linen, for Aaron and his sons,
ESV.28: and the turban of fine linen, and the caps of fine linen, and the linen undergarments of fine twined linen,
ESV.29: and the sash of fine twined linen and of blue and purple and scarlet yarns, embroidered with needlework, as the LORD had commanded Moses.
ESV.30: They made the plate of the holy crown of pure gold, and wrote on it an inscription, like the engraving of a signet, “Holy to the LORD.”
ESV.31: And they tied to it a cord of blue to fasten it on the turban above, as the LORD had commanded Moses.
ESV.32: Thus all the work of the tabernacle of the tent of meeting was finished, and the people of Israel did according to all that the LORD had commanded Moses; so they did.
ESV.33: Then they brought the tabernacle to Moses, the tent and all its utensils, its hooks, its frames, its bars, its pillars, and its bases;
ESV.34: the covering of tanned rams' skins and goatskins, and the veil of the screen;
ESV.35: the ark of the testimony with its poles and the mercy seat;
ESV.36: the table with all its utensils, and the bread of the Presence;
ESV.37: the lampstand of pure gold and its lamps with the lamps set and all its utensils, and the oil for the light;
ESV.38: the golden altar, the anointing oil and the fragrant incense, and the screen for the entrance of the tent;
ESV.39: the bronze altar, and its grating of bronze, its poles, and all its utensils; the basin and its stand;

NLT.1: The craftsmen made beautiful sacred garments of blue, purple, and scarlet cloth — clothing for Aaron to wear while ministering in the Holy Place, just as the LORD had commanded Moses.
NLT.2: Bezalel made the ephod of finely woven linen and embroidered it with gold and with blue, purple, and scarlet thread.
NLT.3: He made gold thread by hammering out thin sheets of gold and cutting it into fine strands. With great skill and care, he worked it into the fine linen with the blue, purple, and scarlet thread.
NLT.4: The ephod consisted of two pieces, front and back, joined at the shoulders with two shoulder-pieces.
NLT.5: The decorative sash was made of the same materials: finely woven linen embroidered with gold and with blue, purple, and scarlet thread, just as the LORD had commanded Moses.
NLT.6: They mounted the two onyx stones in settings of gold filigree. The stones were engraved with the names of the tribes of Israel, just as a seal is engraved.
NLT.7: He fastened these stones on the shoulder-pieces of the ephod as a reminder that the priest represents the people of Israel. All this was done just as the LORD had commanded Moses.
NLT.8: Bezalel made the chestpiece with great skill and care. He made it to match the ephod, using finely woven linen embroidered with gold and with blue, purple, and scarlet thread.
NLT.9: He made the chestpiece of a single piece of cloth folded to form a pouch nine inches square.
NLT.10: They mounted four rows of gemstones on it. The first row contained a red carnelian, a pale-green peridot, and an emerald.
NLT.11: The second row contained a turquoise, a blue lapis lazuli, and a white moonstone.
NLT.12: The third row contained an orange jacinth, an agate, and a purple amethyst.
NLT.13: The fourth row contained a blue-green beryl, an onyx, and a green jasper. All these stones were set in gold filigree.
NLT.14: Each stone represented one of the twelve sons of Israel, and the name of that tribe was engraved on it like a seal.

NLT.16: They also made two settings of gold filigree and two gold rings and attached them to the top corners of the chestpiece.
NLT.17: They tied the two gold cords to the rings on the chestpiece.
NLT.18: They tied the other ends of the cords to the gold settings on the shoulder-pieces of the ephod.
NLT.19: Then they made two more gold rings and attached them to the inside edges of the chestpiece next to the ephod.
NLT.20: Then they made two more gold rings and attached them to the front of the ephod, below the shoulder-pieces, just above the knot where the decorative sash was fastened to the ephod.
NLT.21: They attached the bottom rings of the chestpiece to the rings on the ephod with blue cords. In this way, the chestpiece was held securely to the ephod above the decorative sash. All this was done just as the LORD had commanded Moses.
NLT.22: Bezalel made the robe that is worn with the ephod from a single piece of blue woven cloth,
NLT.23: with an opening for Aaron’s head in the middle of it. The opening was reinforced with a woven collar so it would not tear.
NLT.24: They made pomegranates of blue, purple, and scarlet yarn, and attached them to the hem of the robe.
NLT.25: They also made bells of pure gold and placed them between the pomegranates along the hem of the robe,
NLT.26: with bells and pomegranates alternating all around the hem. This robe was to be worn whenever the priest ministered before the LORD, just as the LORD had commanded Moses.
NLT.27: They made tunics for Aaron and his sons from fine linen cloth.
NLT.28: The turban and the special head coverings were made of fine linen, and the undergarments were also made of finely woven linen.
NLT.29: The sashes were made of finely woven linen and embroidered with blue, purple, and scarlet thread, just as the LORD had commanded Moses.
NLT.30: Finally, they made the sacred medallion — the badge of holiness — of pure gold. They engraved it like a seal with these words: HOLY TO THE LORD.
NLT.31: They attached the medallion with a blue cord to Aaron’s turban, just as the LORD had commanded Moses.
NLT.32: And so at last the Tabernacle was finished. The Israelites had done everything just as the LORD had commanded Moses.
